collection: NERDC JSS 1 Physical and Health Education posture and food preservation
note: Original classroom practice. Independent academic review pending.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.learningObjective: Describe body position using observable features.
questions.prompt: Two pictures show a pupil doing different tasks. In picture A the pupil is seated with the back supported. In picture B the pupil is upright and taking a step forward. Name the posture or activity shown in each and give one visible clue.
questions.answer: A shows sitting, with body weight supported by the seat. B shows walking, with a step in progress.
questions.explanation: Posture describes how the body is held. Body position can be described during stillness or movement.

markingGuide.description: Uses the seat or supported back as evidence.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish a momentary sitting position from evidence of a spinal condition.
questions.prompt: During a lesson, Kemi leans sideways to see the board. A classmate says that this single observation proves Kemi has scoliosis caused by sitting badly. Explain two problems with the claim.
questions.answer: A momentary lean does not establish that the spine has a sideways curve. Sitting badly is not an established cause of idiopathic scoliosis.
questions.explanation: Scoliosis involves a spinal curve. A classroom observation does not replace a clinical assessment, and the cause of idiopathic scoliosis is unknown.

markingGuide.description: Explains why a momentary lean does not establish a spinal curve or diagnosis.
Explains that poor posture does not cause idiopathic scoliosis or that the observation cannot establish a cause.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.learningObjective: Explain how refrigeration helps preserve perishable food.
questions.prompt: The school cook has a portion of cooked stew to save for later. Which choice uses refrigeration to help preserve it?
questions.answer: Refrigerate the stew promptly in a clean covered container.
questions.explanation: Keeping perishable food cold slows the growth of many microorganisms. A cover helps protect the food from contamination.
options: Keep it beside a sunny window until it is needed.
Refrigerate the stew promptly in a clean covered container.
Cover it and leave it at room temperature all afternoon.
Keep it in a warm cupboard to prevent moisture loss.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.learningObjective: Use a food safety temperature criterion to interpret a storage record.
questions.prompt: A canteen checks a refrigerator holding perishable food. Its chart sets a target below 5 °C. Readings are 3 °C at opening and 8 °C later in the morning. Which reading meets the target, and what can staff conclude from the other reading?
questions.answer: The 3 °C reading meets the target. The 8 °C reading shows that the refrigerator was above the target when checked. Staff need to investigate and assess the food under their safety procedure.
questions.explanation: The readings compare measured temperatures with the stated target. They do not give a continuous record of how long the food was above it.

markingGuide.description: Explains that the readings do not establish how long the temperature was too high or that further checks are needed.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.learningObjective: Identify drying from the change made to a food.
questions.prompt: At a market, one supplier sells dried pepper flakes and another sells fresh peppers. What change in the peppers identifies drying as the method used to make the flakes?
questions.answer: Much of the water has been removed from the peppers.
questions.explanation: Drying removes moisture. Lower water availability can slow many processes that spoil food.
options: More water has been mixed into the peppers.
The peppers have been kept below freezing during sale.
The peppers have been stored in a liquid brine.
Much of the water has been removed from the peppers.
